newsitem.title: USA: UAW, Ford resume labor talks, anticipate deal.
newsitem.headline: UAW, Ford resume labor talks, anticipate deal.

text.p: Negotiations between Ford Motor Co. and the United Auto Workers resumed Monday following a break Sunday night that allowed bargainers to rest up for a final push for a new national labor contract.
"I think we're very close to a settlement," Ford spokesman Jon Harmon said. "Rest was a good thing, and now we're optimistic we're going to have a settlement today."

Worries of a strike remained low as production at Ford's U.S. parts and assembly plants resumed on normal schedules, Harmon said. The past three-year labor contract covering the automaker's 105,000 UAW hourly workers expired at midnight on Saturday.
Ford Chairman Alex Trotman was scheduled to meet with reporters at 11 a.m. EDT, prior to a previously scheduled speech to the Economic Club of Detroit.
UAW officials said the two sides were close to an agreement, but still at odds over key outsourcing issues.

In the pact affecting hourly workers, the union has sought to guarantee minimum employment levels and provisions that restrict the company's ability to shift work to outside suppliers, including establishing the right to strike over such decisions.

Also on the table was the length of time it takes for new workers to reach wage parity with veteran workers. In the previous pact, new hires started at 70 percent of the full, $19-an-hour wage, catching up to veteran workers after three years on the job.

Ford and UAW sources also confirmed Sunday that they reached a tentative agreement covering about 750 salaried workers represented by the union, including designers and product development employees. Details of that agreement were not immediately available.

The New York Times on Monday quoted an unidentifed source as saying that the union had scheduled a board meeting to approve a proposed contract. A UAW spokesman was not immediately available for comment on the report.
